newsitem.title: USA: Elsag Bailey CEO comfortable with EPS range.
newsitem.headline: Elsag Bailey CEO comfortable with EPS range.

text.p: The chief executive of Elsag Bailey Process Automation NV said Wednesday he was comfortable with the range of estimates for second-quarter earnings per share.
"There is a range," the executive, Vincenzo Cannatelli, said in a Reuter interview. "I'm comfortable with the range in the market today."
The First Call EPS estimates from analysts range from $0.31 to $0.43. The consensus is $0.37, against EPS of $0.40 for the same period the year before.
About half of Elsag Bailey's earnings come from Europe, and Canatelli said the recent weakening of European currencies -- especially the German mark -- against the dollar would affect EPS slightly.
"We probably calculate the impact on EPS ... should not be more than three to four cents a share on a quarterly basis," said Canatelli, who is also the company's managing director.

Asked about the consensus estimate of $1.57 EPS for 1997, Cannatelli said, "What we said to the market at the beginning of 1997 was that it would be a consolidation and stabilization year. We are still on track on that."

Elsag Bailey, a Netherlands company, had EPS of $1.53 in 1996. The company supplies automation instrumentation, analytical products, control systems and services to such industries as power utilities, oil and gas, pulp and paper and metals.
Cannatelli said revenues could grow five to six percent a year -- about 1.5 times the rate of the market's growth -- without acquisitions. Elsag Bailey had 1996 revenues of $1.6 billion.
He said his goal was to increase EPS to $3 a year by the end of 2000, adding, "I think we can substantially improve this (EPS) in the next three years."

He said Elsag Bailey was seeing results from its $700 acquisition of Germany's Hartmann & Braun in 1996. The cost of restructuring, including the layoffs of 2,000 workers and closing plants, was $120 million to $130 million.

However, the merger had helped cut research and development costs to $80 million a year from a combined $95 million. The combined companies' operating margin reached eight percent last year and the goal is to hit 10 to 12 percent.
Canatelli said the company had seen a "nice pickup" in European orders during the first half of 1997, and Germany's economy was starting to gain strength.
"We should start to see good progress in the 1998-99 time frame, after a slow '95 and '96," he said. "1997 is a transition year."
Elsag Bailey is controlled by Italy's Finmeccanica SpA .
